Top candidates: Leaf_Mold (yellow spots upper surface), Powdery_Mildew (dusty coating), Early_Blight (spots with rings), Septoria_Leaf_Blotch (small circular spots). Viewing one reference from each.

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Tomato leaf with discrete yellow/pale spots scattered across the upper surface on a dark green background. No large brown lesions, no distinct concentric rings, no white powdery uniform coating.

- **Leaf_Mold ref**: Shows pale/yellowish discrete spots on upper leaf surface — very similar pattern to test image.
- **Powdery_Mildew ref**: Shows a more uniform whitish powdery coating — less similar; test image has discrete spots, not a diffuse coating.
- **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch ref**: Shows small, defined dark/gray circular spots — the test image spots are yellowish/pale, not dark gray circles.
- **Early_Blight ref**: Shows large dark brown lesions with clear concentric rings — clearly not matching.

The test image best matches **Leaf_Mold**: discrete pale greenish-yellow spots on upper leaf surface, consistent with indistinct chlorotic margins and upper-surface spotting before the olive mold becomes prominent on the underside.
